# Plan: Build the opening environment and terminal

## Design

Source context: `index.html` has `#app` and loads `src/main.ts`; `three` is in `package.json`; `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` serves the build under `/signal-lost/`; `.swarm/architecture.md` names the `app`, `render`, `terminal`, and `input` modules.

- `src/app/scenes.ts`: DOM-free `createSceneManager()`. A `Scene` has `mount(): void` and `dispose(): void`. `show(scene)` disposes the current scene before mounting the next one; `dispose()` tears down the current one. Pure, unit-tested.
- `src/app/opening.ts`: opening scene. Prints the design's SIGNAL RECEIVED text line by line, then the prompt. Enter or a click at any time moves on. Removes its listeners on dispose.
- `src/app/hub.ts`: boot sequence and terminal hub. Prints the OBSERVER NETWORK boot text, then a numbered tool menu from a `Tool[]` list. Tools are `{ id, label, run }`. This WorkUnit ships only real ones (`STATUS`, `HELP`); later WorkUnits add theirs. No placeholder entries.
- `src/terminal/terminal.ts`: DOM terminal. `print(lines)`, `menu(items)`, and a command input. Output goes in a `role="log"` `aria-live="polite"` element as real text. Menu items are buttons, also chosen by typing the number or name.
- `src/render/environment.ts`: Three.js scene, loaded by dynamic import so text appears before the 3D code does. Starfield `Points`, a flat-shaded low-poly icosahedron with a ring, a moving analyzer sweep line, low-resolution rendering with pixelated CSS scaling, vertex snapping by `onBeforeCompile`. `createEnvironment(canvas, { motion })` returns `{ start, stop, setMotion, dispose }`, or throws when WebGL is unavailable. Rendering stops when the document is hidden and on `stop`/`dispose`, which also disposes geometries, materials and the renderer. `motion: false` renders one still frame.
- `src/main.ts`: bootstraps. If the environment throws, it sets `document.body.dataset.render = 'fallback'` and shows a CSS-only static starfield; otherwise `'webgl'`. The game continues either way.
- `src/style.css`: CRT bezel, amber phosphor, subtle scanlines and vignette, and periodic interference as a CSS animation on an overlay. System monospace stack, because no font asset is in the repo.

## Text

The opening text is specified verbatim in the maintainer's brief; the boot text is new copy proposed here. Both are the fictional software's fixed interface output, so they live in `src/app/text.ts`. Story content starts in the Episode 000 WorkUnit.

Opening (from the brief):

    SIGNAL RECEIVED
    ORIGIN: UNKNOWN
    CLASSIFICATION: UNRESOLVED
    CONFIDENCE: 0.0031%

    ADDITIONAL OBSERVERS REQUIRED.

    PRESS ENTER TO JOIN THE NETWORK

Boot (proposal):

    OBSERVER NETWORK CLIENT 2.3
    CHECKING WORK QUEUE ......... 1 UNIT
    PEERS REACHABLE ............. 0
    SYSTEM CLOCK ................ 2001
    TOOLS AVAILABLE TO THIS OBSERVER:

## Lifecycle ownership

- `main.ts` owns the one render host for the whole session. It creates it once and disposes it on `pagehide`. Scenes never create or dispose the renderer. They only choose its layout through `document.body.dataset.scene` (`opening`, `hub`), which CSS uses to size the canvas; a `ResizeObserver` in `environment.ts` tracks the result.
- `src/render/host.ts` (DOM-free): `createRenderHost(load)` calls an injected async loader. If `dispose()` happens before the import resolves, the environment is disposed as soon as it arrives and never started. Load failure calls `onFailure`, which `main.ts` uses for the fallback.
- `src/render/loop.ts` (DOM-free): `createLoop({ draw, schedule, cancel })` with `start`, `stop`, `setMotion`, `setVisible`, `dispose`. No frame is scheduled when stopped, hidden, motion-off, or disposed. Motion-off draws one still frame.
- Scenes own their own timers and listeners, cleared in `dispose`. The `Terminal` is owned by whichever scene mounted it.

## Files

New: `src/app/{scenes,opening,hub,text}.ts`, `src/render/{host,loop}.ts`, `src/terminal/terminal.ts`, `src/render/environment.ts`, `src/style.css`, `tests/unit/{scenes,render}.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`. Changed: `src/main.ts`, `index.html` only if the stylesheet link needs it, `tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` (the old text expectation still applies), `playwright.config.ts` (add a software WebGL launch flag so tests can exercise the real renderer).

## Edge cases

- Enter pressed before the opening finishes still boots.
- WebGL failing at context creation shows the fallback with no uncaught error.
- A dynamic-import or render failure also uses the fallback.
- Resizing updates the renderer size.

## Out of scope

Puzzles, audio, persistence, settings UI.

# Test plan

| Acceptance criterion | Verification | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opening shows starfield, rotating object, sweep, interference and the text, ending in the prompt | `tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`: text and prompt visible, `body[data-render=webgl]`, canvas has non-blank pixels, interference overlay present. Source inspection: rotation updates per frame, sweep position moves per frame, the interference CSS animation repeats, and the renderer uses a pixel ratio below 1 with `image-rendering: pixelated`. The exact opening text sequence is asserted. | Developer on host; CI `Browser tests` |
| Enter or click boots into a terminal with a tool menu | `opening.spec.ts`, once with Enter and once with click, then a menu button works and a typed command works | Developer on host; CI |
| WebGL failure shows a styled fallback and stays playable | `opening.spec.ts` forces `getContext` to return null by init script: `data-render=fallback`, no page errors, boot works, then a menu button and a typed command each produce readable output | Developer on host; CI |
| Lifecycle mounts and disposes scenes, rendering stops when not needed | `npx vitest run tests/unit/scenes.test.ts tests/unit/render.test.ts`: mount order, replacement disposes first, final disposal; no frames scheduled when stopped, hidden, motion-off or disposed; a host disposed before its import resolves never starts | Developer; tester inspects |
| Browser tests cover opening, boot, fallback under the subpath | `fixtures.ts` returns 404 outside `/signal-lost/`; `opening.spec.ts` uses it | CI |

Browser command: `npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`. It runs on the host and in CI, never as a sandbox implementation dependency.

## Roles

- **Developer:** runs focused commands above and `npm run lint`. Browser specs run on the host session, as sandboxes cannot start Chromium (`.swarm/rules/lessons.md`).
- **Tester:** independently inspects source against the criteria, reuses applicable passing results, repeats only for relevant changes, failures, or unresolved coverage.
- **Coordinator:** alone runs the complete required policy. The `Browser tests` workflow on the PR is the browser evidence.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED

The proposed implementation covers the WorkUnit's functional scope, but its copy placement conflicts with the approved content boundary and its claimed source for the opening copy is not verifiable.

| Contract area | Audit | Evidence / disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opening visuals and text | Covered, with source clarification required | PLAN.md specifies stars, rotating geometry, sweep, repeating interference and the final prompt. TEST_PLAN.md combines browser assertions with inspection of animation code. See R2 for the claimed verbatim copy. |
| Enter/click boot and interactive terminal | Covered | Opening listeners, hub, button menu and typed commands have explicit browser verification for both entry methods. STATUS/HELP keep this WorkUnit independent of puzzles. |
| WebGL fallback and continued playability | Covered | Forced context failure, styled static fallback, absence of page errors and working button/typed commands are planned. |
| Scene lifecycle and rendering shutdown | Covered | Scene replacement/disposal, frame cancellation when stopped/hidden/disposed, motion-off behavior and late async-load disposal have focused unit coverage. Main owns the renderer; scenes own terminal instances, timers and listeners. |
| Browser coverage under Pages subpath | Covered | Existing tests/e2e/fixtures.ts rejects paths outside /signal-lost/; playwright.config.ts uses that base URL. New specs reuse that fixture. |
| Low-resolution flat-shaded rendering; restrained effects | Covered | Low-resolution pixelated output, flat-shaded geometry and lightweight overlays fit the constraint. Keep the proposed vertex snapping inexpensive. |
| Real readable DOM output and aria-live | Design covered | Terminal uses DOM text, role=log, aria-live=polite, buttons and input. Add explicit accessibility inspection to the test plan as recommended below. |
| Content/engine separation | Revision required | PLAN.md places authored opening and boot output in src/app/text.ts; SYSTEM_PROMPT.md requires player-facing text in content/ except fixed interface labels. See R1. |
| Scope, dependencies and protected paths | Covered | No puzzles, audio, backend or new dependency is proposed. Three.js is already in package.json. Listed source/test/config changes are outside protected paths. |
| Validation ownership and environment | Covered | Developer owns focused unit checks and lint; tester independently inspects/reuses results; coordinator owns full trusted-base validation. Browser evidence comes from a capable host/PR CI and is not a sandbox implementation prerequisite. |

## Required revisions

### R1 — Preserve the approved content boundary

Move the authored opening and boot blocks into a declarative file under content/ and update the exact file list and loading approach. Fixed controls such as HELP or STATUS may remain interface labels in source. The multi-line atmospheric output, including origin/classification/confidence and fictional boot diagnostics, should not be treated wholesale as fixed labels. Keep the existing prose unchanged while moving it; no expansion into episode or puzzle content is needed. Update TEST_PLAN.md to verify that this content loads under /signal-lost/ and that the terminal renders it as DOM text.

### R2 — Distinguish sourced requirements from proposed copy

PLAN.md says the opening is specified verbatim in a maintainer brief. WORKUNIT.md requires SIGNAL RECEIVED and the final PRESS ENTER TO JOIN THE NETWORK prompt, but does not supply the intermediate lines. docs/game-design.md contains no opening block or SIGNAL RECEIVED passage. REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md repeats the plan and test plan; it supplies no independent brief, prior verdict or additional lesson supporting that claim. Cite an available, verifiable approved source for the intermediate copy, or label those lines as proposed copy consistent with the contract. Do not make implementation depend on locating an unavailable brief. The existing source-context claims about index.html, package.json, the fixture and architecture were independently verified.

## Recommended verification clarification

Add a focused browser/source inspection step checking the log's aria-live semantics, readable DOM output, keyboard focus after boot and visible focus for menu/input controls. This verifies existing accessibility requirements without adding a new feature or requiring a new dependency.

## Handoff

Revise PLAN.md and TEST_PLAN.md for R1–R2, retaining the current module ownership and focused-check split. No implementation tests were run for this plan audit. Prior artifacts were treated as advisory evidence; this review does not change the WorkUnit's configured plan gate of none or authorize harness changes.
